comment: Why: the baseline theme is the one every new player meets first (sector 0 is always gravity), so its table has to be survivable at threat 1 and still scale. Its flavour is weight: armour that was left standing, bats that let go of the ceiling, ogres whose footsteps are the warning, and one big Ravager for a party that is too loud. The construct faction is thin at threat 1, so the entries of the early bands name the Living Armor directly.
description: Deepslate halls under a heavy ceiling: constructs, brutes and what falls from above. The baseline theme and the first sector a player ever sees, so it is gentle at threat 1 and very heavy by threat 8.

entries.comment: A sentry or two of the construct tag (our Living Armors first): armour that was left standing. The faction is fixed to constructs because gravity halls are the home of weight and metal.
Slimes that slid in from the cracks: weight-bags that teach the party to look down. Only up to threat 6, after which they are not worth a roll.

The signature standard encounter of the baseline theme: a march of Living Armors. The id is explicit (not the faction) so that the first sector, whose construct window is thin, still has a reliable fight.
Falling stone turned into creatures: bats that roost in the vaults let go of the dark when the party passes under them. Spread over three places, short hunt.
Heavy walkers of the ogre tag arriving as one group with a slow, audible approach (the cue is their footsteps). A gravity hall is where the big, slow things live.
The lone hunter of this theme: one brute of the ogre tag, only for a party in the dark. Heavy things stalk by feel, not by sight.
Constructs that wake only in light: their visors catch a torch. Carrying light in a gravity hall is a trade, not a gift.

Tensura's war gnomes in a squad. The id is explicit because the ogre tag mixes them with weaker things and the brigade is meant to be a recognisable fight. It ends at threat 12, where the ogre tag draws something tougher than a gnome.

The loud brute: a Ravager (100 health, five points of budget on its own) comes to a noisy party. It is the most expensive single thing in the table, so it is hard band only and from threat 3, where a hard budget (19 and more) can pay for it.

The mimic-style surprise of the baseline theme: the statue on its plinth steps down, an iron golem (100 health) with a Living Armor or two at its heels. Close range and a short hunt, because the point is that it was there all along.
A giant bear: the heavy beast of the table. Hard because it is one big body rather than a crowd; a larger party meets more than one.
The ambush of the baseline theme: an armour column and one brute, arriving in three places while a cloud of dust marks where something fell. The message is the only warning.
The late ambush: a march of ogres and constructs. Only for parties of two or more, because a solo player meeting it is not a fight but a funeral.
